useCases.title: Cross-Border Micro-Credentials: The EU.ACE Chain (EU - CH)
useCases.summary:
1. Delivery. Participants complete a 1 ECTS programme (EQF 6-7; 60% pass grade, 80% attendance).

2. Modelling. SAPIO models it in an EDC/ELM-aligned structure — holder, activity, assessment, achievement — with nested learning outcomes. The template is reusable across the alliance.

3. Issuer identity. The university is registered as a trusted entity via institutional DID and X.509, making it the cryptographic root of trust rather than the platform.

4. Issuance. The academic coordinator supplies the eligible cohort; SAPIO generates OID4VCI offers. Opt-in — declining carries no academic consequence.

5. Retrieval. The learner accepts in a standards-compliant wallet. No proprietary app, no SAPIO account, no personal data retained afterwards.

6. Presentation. The learner presents over OID4VP, disclosing only the claims the verifier needs.

7. Verification. The relying party validates against the university's key material in seconds — with no relationship to SAPIO, no prior agreement with the university, and no marginal cost per re-verification.
useCases.userJourney:
1. Programme delivery. Participants complete "Education for All — Empowering Higher Education through Quality Micro-Credentials" (16-27 March 2026, English, 1 ECTS, EQF 6-7). Academic requirements: 60% pass grade, 80% attendance.

2. Credential modelling. SAPIO models the programme in an EDC/ELM-aligned structure — holder, activity, assessment, achievement — with nested learning outcomes under Knowledge, Skills and Competences. The template is programme-agnostic and reusable across the alliance without redesign.

3. Issuer identity. The awarding institution is established as an institutional DID with an X.509 certificate, registered as a trusted entity. From here the university, not the platform, is the cryptographic root of trust.

4. Issuance. The academic coordinator supplies the list of participants who met the criteria. SAPIO generates OID4VCI credential offers. Participation is voluntary and opt-in; declining has no effect on academic standing.
